requirements.requirement: usb-storage module is prevented from loading immediately (now)
requirements.summary: Baseline confirmed usb_storage was not loaded but was loadable (modinfo succeeded). Executor created /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-usb-storage.conf with both a 'blacklist' directive and an 'install ... /bin/false' hard-block, then directly verified 'sudo modprobe usb_storage' fails with exit code 1 immediately after the file was created.

requirements.requirement: usb-storage module remains blocked from loading after a reboot (persistence)
requirements.summary: Executor rebuilt initramfs for the running kernel so the blacklist applies at early boot, captured a pre-reboot boot_id, then issued a real reboot which was acknowledged and caused a connectivity gap (timeout on one poll, success on next). Post-reboot boot_id differed from pre-reboot boot_id, directly confirming a real restart occurred (cross-checked by the fixed global before/after boot-identity snapshots, showing the same before value 242af11e... and after value 09bc3fe9...). After reconnecting, lsmod confirmed usb_storage was not loaded and 'sudo modprobe usb_storage' still failed with the same /bin/false-driven error, and the blacklist config file was intact, directly demonstrating the block survived the full disruption/restore cycle.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — blocking usb_storage from loading immediately and ensuring it stays blocked after reboot — are directly and coherently satisfied. The executor established a healthy pre-change baseline, applied a robust blacklist+install-false configuration, rebuilt initramfs, performed and verified an actual reboot (boot_id change corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots), and re-verified the block and file persistence post-reboot. Hygiene is very good; the only minor blemish is an unreviewed /tmp/reboot.log left from the backgrounded reboot command.
limitations: The post-reboot verification window is brief (single check immediately after reconnect); no extended-uptime recheck was captured, though this is a reasonable bound for this task.
It is not confirmed whether /tmp/reboot.log survived the reboot or was cleared, since it was not checked post-reboot.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map cleanly to the task: creating the blacklist/install config file (required deliverable), rebuilding initramfs (necessary for early-boot persistence), and rebooting node1 (necessary to prove persistence, and doubling as the required provider-wide restart-evidence protocol). No unrelated services were touched, no failed units appeared before or after (global:before_prepare:node1:failed-services and global:after_executor:node1:failed-services both empty), package health remained consistent (dpkg reported clean both times), and listening sockets are unchanged in substance (only PID/ephemeral churn from the reboot). One minor, low-risk residue: the reboot command redirected output to /tmp/reboot.log via 'nohup ... >/tmp/reboot.log 2>&1 &' (cmd-6d26dd8b7f224390); this was never inspected or cleaned up post-reboot, though it is trivial, non-sensitive, and likely cleared by /tmp's normal boot-time cleanup. No troubleshooting experiments or abandoned mutations were observed.
